Definition: from a compound of G2411 and the base of G2041; to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively):--minister.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, hierourgéō means to minister as a priest. It occurs just once, in Romans.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple here: hierourgéō means to minister as a priest, and I do not stretch it further.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
